tests.title: Unit 4: Supply and Market Equilibrium – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: A farmer holds back part of his harvest because he expects prices to rise next month. This causes current supply to:
options: Remain unchanged, as supply depends only on cost
Rise, because of higher expected profit
Fall, because he withholds stock from the market
Become perfectly elastic at the present price
questions.explanation: Expectation of higher future prices reduces current supply.

questions.question_text: Which of the following will shift the supply curve of cotton shirts to the right?
options: A rise in the wages of garment workers
An excise duty on cotton shirts
A rise in the price of cotton shirts
questions.explanation: Cheaper production raises supply at each price; a price rise only moves along the curve.

questions.question_text: An excise duty imposed on a good will:
options: Shift the supply curve to the right
Leave supply unchanged but raise demand
Shift the supply curve to the left
questions.explanation: It raises cost per unit, so less is supplied at each price.

questions.question_text: A subsidy on fertiliser for farmers causes the supply curve of wheat to:
The law of supply states that, ceteris paribus, quantity supplied:
questions.explanation: Direct relation between price and quantity supplied.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an exception to the law of supply?
options: Supply of cotton cloth by competitive mills in the short run
Supply of manufactured goods in a factory with idle capacity
Labour supply at very high wages when workers prefer leisure
Supply of bread by bakeries facing rising flour prices

questions.question_text: At Rs 20 a firm supplies 100 units and at Rs 25 it supplies 120. The market has three identical firms. Market supply at Rs 25 is:
The supply curve of a competitive firm in the short run is its:
options: MC curve above the minimum of AVC
questions.explanation: The firm supplies where P = MC, provided P covers AVC.

questions.question_text: A rise in the price of an input used by a firm will:
options: Cause a movement up the supply curve
questions.explanation: Higher cost reduces supply at each price.

questions.question_text: Expansion of supply occurs when:
options: The cost of production of the good falls for all firms
A per-unit subsidy is given to producers of the good
Technology used by the producers improves over time
The own price of the good rises, other things unchanged
questions.explanation: It is an upward movement along the same curve.

questions.question_text: A change in technology that lowers cost causes:
questions.explanation: The whole supply curve shifts right.

questions.question_text: Which of the following changes the QUANTITY SUPPLIED (not supply)?
options: A change in the rate of tax on the product
A change in the price of the good itself
A change in the technology used for production
A change in the prices of inputs used in it
questions.explanation: Only the good's own price causes movement along the curve.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes "substitutes in production"?
options: Goods that are used together by consumers, such as tea and sugar
Goods that are sold at the same price in a competitive market
Goods that can replace one another in the consumer's budget
Goods made from the same resources, such as wheat and barley
questions.explanation: A rise in the price of one reduces supply of the other.

questions.question_text: If the price of wheat rises sharply, the supply of barley (a substitute in production) will:
The supply curve is upward sloping chiefly because:
options: Firms usually enjoy increasing returns to scale as they expand
Fixed costs of production are spread over a larger output
Marginal cost rises with output, so a higher price must be offered
Consumers buy larger quantities when the price of a good falls

questions.question_text: A perfectly inelastic supply curve is:
questions.explanation: Quantity supplied is fixed whatever the price.

questions.question_text: The price elasticity of supply of an old painting by a deceased master is:
When price rises from Rs 10 to Rs 12 and quantity supplied rises from 100 to 130, Es is:
When price rises from Rs 50 to Rs 55 and supply rises from 200 to 204, supply is:
A straight-line supply curve passing through the origin has elasticity:
questions.explanation: At every point P/Q is equal to the slope.

questions.question_text: A straight-line supply curve that cuts the Y-axis (price axis) has elasticity:
questions.explanation: The positive price intercept makes it elastic.

questions.question_text: A straight-line supply curve that cuts the X-axis (quantity axis) has elasticity:
questions.explanation: The positive quantity intercept makes it inelastic.

questions.question_text: Supply is more elastic in the long run than in the short run because:
options: Costs of production fall automatically as time passes
Incomes of consumers rise over time, raising the demand for goods
Prices of outputs are fixed by the government for longer periods
All inputs can be varied and new firms can enter the industry
questions.explanation: More time allows fuller adjustment of output.

questions.question_text: Which of the following goods is likely to have the most inelastic supply in the short run?
options: Plastic buckets made with idle machines
Bread from a bakery with extra ovens
Cotton shirts produced in a factory with spare capacity
Fresh milk from existing dairy cattle
questions.explanation: Supply of agricultural goods and perishables cannot adjust quickly.

questions.question_text: Perishable goods have inelastic supply because:
options: Consumers do not demand them in large quantities
The government controls their production through licences
They cannot be stored long and output cannot quickly be changed
Their prices are always higher than those of durable goods
questions.explanation: Stock cannot be held back or quickly expanded.

tests.title: Unit 4: Supply and Market Equilibrium – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes market equilibrium?
options: Price is at the lowest level that sellers will ever accept
Demand exceeds supply, so the price is bid up by buyers
Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied at the market price
Supply exceeds demand, so the price is pushed down by sellers

questions.question_text: At Rs 15 quantity demanded is 100 and quantity supplied is 160. The market has:
options: Excess supply of 60, so price will fall
Excess demand of 60, so price will rise

questions.question_text: At Rs 6 quantity demanded is 70 and quantity supplied is 40. The market has:
options: Excess demand of 70, so price will rise
Excess supply of 30, so price will fall
Excess demand of 30, so price will rise
Equilibrium, since both quantities are positive

questions.question_text: Qd = 100 − 5P and Qs = 20 + 3P. Equilibrium price and quantity are:
Qd = 80 − 2P and Qs = 3P − 20. Equilibrium price is:
For Qd = 60 − 2P and Qs = 3P − 10, equilibrium quantity is:
If demand increases and supply is unchanged, equilibrium price and quantity:
questions.explanation: The demand curve shifts right along the supply curve.

questions.question_text: If supply increases and demand is unchanged, equilibrium price and quantity:
Both demand and supply increase. Equilibrium quantity:
questions.explanation: Quantity definitely rises; price depends on relative shifts.

questions.question_text: Demand increases and supply decreases. Equilibrium price:
questions.explanation: Both effects push price up; quantity is uncertain.

questions.question_text: Demand decreases and supply increases. Equilibrium price:
Demand and supply both increase by the same proportion. Equilibrium price:
A price ceiling set below the equilibrium price causes:
options: No effect on the market, since price is the same
A shortage, and a possible black market for the good
A rise in supply, as firms expand to meet demand
A surplus, since producers supply more at the lower price

questions.question_text: A price floor set above the equilibrium price (such as an MSP) causes:
A minimum wage set above the equilibrium wage in a competitive labour market tends to cause:
options: No change in employment, since wages do not matter
A rise in labour demand, since workers are better paid
Unemployment, since labour supplied exceeds labour demanded
A shortage of labour, since firms demand more workers

questions.question_text: The "invisible hand" refers to:
options: Regulation of prices and output by the government
Central planning of production by a committee of experts
Self-interested actions guided by prices serving social good
Control of the market by a single large monopoly seller
questions.explanation: Adam Smith's idea of market coordination.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of a stable equilibrium?
options: Price keeps moving away after any small disturbance
Market forces restore the price after a disturbance
The price of the good is always equal to its cost
The demand curve is vertical at the market price

questions.question_text: At a price above equilibrium, market forces will tend to:
questions.explanation: Excess supply leads to competition among sellers.

questions.question_text: The price mechanism allocates scarce resources mainly through:
questions.explanation: Prices signal scarcity and guide choices.

questions.question_text: Which statement is TRUE about black markets?
options: They arise when ceilings create excess demand at the legal price
They tend to push the prices of controlled goods down
They eliminate the shortage caused by the price control
They arise when government prices are far too high for buyers

questions.question_text: If the government imposes an MSP above equilibrium and buys the surplus, the surplus stock is:
questions.explanation: It must absorb the excess supply.

questions.question_text: Demand shifts rightward by 20 units at every price while supply is unchanged. If supply is perfectly elastic, then:
options: Price falls, and the quantity traded also falls
Price rises by a large amount, quantity rising little
Quantity rises by 20 with no change in price
Neither price nor the quantity traded changes at all
questions.explanation: A horizontal supply curve means quantity absorbs the shift.

questions.question_text: If supply is perfectly inelastic (vertical) and demand rises:
options: Quantity rises by the same proportion as demand
Price falls as the extra demand is not served
Price and quantity stay as they were before
Price rises and the quantity traded is unchanged

questions.question_text: An increase in income raises demand for a normal good, raising equilibrium price. The extent of the price rise is larger when supply is:
questions.explanation: A steep supply curve gives a larger price change.

questions.question_text: A tax on sellers is borne more by buyers when:
options: Supply is perfectly elastic and demand is elastic
questions.explanation: Buyers who cannot easily substitute bear more.

tests.title: Unit 4: Supply and Market Equilibrium – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: A tax on a good with perfectly inelastic supply is borne:
questions.explanation: Sellers cannot reduce quantity or shift the burden.

questions.question_text: If demand is perfectly elastic, the burden of a tax on sellers falls:
questions.explanation: Buyers will not pay a higher price.

questions.question_text: Supply is "unitary elastic" when:
A firm's marginal cost curve slopes upward because of:
questions.explanation: More output requires more of the variable factor with falling productivity.

questions.question_text: If the price of a good is less than AVC, the firm in the short run should:
Which of the following would NOT shift the supply curve of tea?
options: A change in the price of tea
A change in the cost of labour
questions.explanation: Price changes move along the curve.

questions.question_text: A drought reduces supply of a crop. With inelastic demand, the equilibrium price will:
questions.explanation: Quantity is scarce and buyers cannot switch.

questions.question_text: Which of the following indicates an increase in supply?
options: The firm sells more at each price because costs fell
The firm sells the same quantity at the same price
The firm sells less at each price because costs rose
The firm sells more because the price of the good rose

questions.question_text: The market supply is the:
options: Sum of quantities supplied by all firms at each price
Quantity supplied by the largest firm in the market
Average of the quantities supplied by individual firms
Sum of the prices charged by all firms in the market

questions.question_text: Market supply curve is flatter than a single firm's because:
options: More firms supply more at each price

questions.question_text: If the elasticity of supply is 2 and price rises by 10%, quantity supplied rises by:
A bumper wheat crop lowers price. Farmers' income may fall because demand is:
questions.explanation: Price falls proportionately more than quantity rises.

questions.question_text: The incidence of a tax on a good depends on the relative:
options: Costs of collecting the tax from the sellers
Prices of the good and of its main substitute
Quantities bought and sold before the tax
Elasticities of demand and supply of the good
questions.explanation: The less elastic side bears more.

questions.question_text: The "economic rent" earned by a factor is the surplus over its:
questions.explanation: The minimum needed to keep it in current use.

questions.question_text: The supply of land as a whole is considered perfectly inelastic because:
options: Land has no alternative uses and so earns no rent
Its total quantity is fixed by nature and cannot grow
Land is highly mobile between regions and sectors
Land is a cheap input in most production processes

questions.question_text: In a competitive market, if firms earn supernormal profit in the short run, in the long run:
options: More firms enter and price falls

questions.question_text: If a market is in equilibrium and a new technology reduces cost for all producers, then equilibrium price and quantity will:
An increase in the price of a complement of good X will:
options: Lower demand for X, reducing its price and quantity
Raise the price of X as buyers switch to it
Leave X unaffected as the goods are unrelated
Raise the supply of X as producers make more

questions.question_text: The equilibrium price of a good rises and the quantity falls. This can be due to:
Equilibrium price falls and quantity falls. This indicates:
Equilibrium quantity rises while price is unchanged. This indicates:
options: Supply decreased while demand remained unchanged
Demand decreased while supply remained unchanged
Demand increased while supply remained unchanged
Demand and supply both increased by the same proportion

questions.question_text: If an MSP is fixed Rs 5 above equilibrium and farmers produce more, the surplus is:
options: Zero, because the government buys all the output
Equal to the total demand at the new price
Negative, because demand now exceeds the supply
The gap between supply and demand at the MSP

questions.question_text: Rent control is an example of:
A subsidy of Rs 2 per unit to sellers shifts the supply curve:
options: Not at all, because it affects only demand
To a vertical line at the current output
Down by Rs 2, or equivalently to the right
Up by Rs 2, or equivalently to the left
questions.explanation: Cost per unit falls by the subsidy.

questions.question_text: A per-unit tax of Rs 3 shifts the supply curve:

tests.title: Unit 4: Supply and Market Equilibrium – Practice Test 4

questions.question_text: Quantity demanded is 200 and quantity supplied is 150 at the controlled price. The shortage is:
Which describes an unstable equilibrium?
options: A disturbance pushes the price further from equilibrium
The supply curve is vertical at the equilibrium price
The demand curve is horizontal at the equilibrium price
A disturbance is corrected and the price returns quickly

questions.question_text: Which of these would the "cobweb" model explain?
options: Incidence of an indirect tax on a consumer good
Pricing decisions by a monopoly with market power
Price fluctuations for crops with a production lag
Permanently stable prices of manufactured goods

questions.question_text: Elasticity of supply of a firm with idle capacity and unemployed resources is likely to be:
Elasticity of supply tends to be lower when:
A good is produced under conditions of rising marginal cost. Its supply curve is:
questions.explanation: Higher price is needed to cover higher MC.

questions.question_text: If demand is unit elastic and supply increases, total revenue of sellers:
questions.explanation: Revenue is constant along unit-elastic demand.

questions.question_text: Which of these is an example of a price floor?
options: Maximum retail price of life-saving drugs

questions.question_text: An MSP is effective only if it is:
With a price ceiling, which group may gain?
options: Suppliers, who receive a lower price but sell more
Buyers who obtain the good at the controlled price
Black marketers, who are the only ones to gain
No one, since all the groups are made worse off

questions.question_text: The effect of a price ceiling set above the equilibrium price is:
Equilibrium price will be higher after a sales tax when:
In the short run, the supply curve of a perfectly competitive firm is vertical when:
Which of the following contributes to price stability in a market?
options: Persistent excess supply at the going price
Self-correcting forces of demand and supply
Binding price controls that remove the incentive to produce
Persistent excess demand at the going price
questions.explanation: Equilibrium is restored by market forces.

questions.question_text: If the supply of a good is Qs = 2P − 10, supply at P = 20 is:
For Qs = 2P − 10, the price at which supply is zero is:
The minimum price at which a firm is willing to supply a product is its:
options: Supply price, based on the marginal cost of the unit
Total fixed cost spread over the planned output
Profit margin as a percentage of the selling price
Marginal revenue at the profit-maximising output
questions.explanation: Supply price covers the cost of the marginal unit.

questions.question_text: When the price of a product rises 5% and supply rises 15%, supply is:
A decrease in the price of a good will cause:
A firm is a price taker. If the market price falls below its minimum AVC, it will supply:
In long-run equilibrium under perfect competition, price equals:
options: Average revenue less the cost of the marginal unit
Zero, since all supernormal profits are competed away
Average fixed cost at the output the firm produces
Marginal cost and the minimum of long-run average cost

questions.question_text: The market supply of a good will fall if:
options: More firms enter the industry in the long run
Technology improves for most of the producers
Producers expect higher future prices and hold back output
Input prices fall for all of the producers

questions.question_text: Which of the following best explains why supply is more inelastic in agriculture?
options: Output can be changed quickly in response to the price
Inputs such as land are available in unlimited amounts
Production depends on weather and takes time to complete
Farmers hold very large stocks of unsold produce

questions.question_text: The demand curve for a good shifts right and the supply curve is vertical. The adjustment is entirely through:
A rise in the price of a substitute for good X and a fall in the cost of producing X will cause equilibrium quantity of X to:
